chunks: And by this isnad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him),
he said: If the water is the measure of a kurr, nothing can make it impure.

key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water — standing or collected water subject to tahara (ritual purity) rulings in Shia jurisprudence
key_terms.كُرٍّ: kurr — a defined unit of water volume in Islamic law; the minimum threshold above which collected water resists ritual impurity regardless of contact with najasah
key_terms.يُنَجِّسْهُ: makes it impure — from Form II verb najjasa, meaning to render ritually defiled (najis); the jussive after lam negates this effect

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia Islamic ruling on kur water — can water that reaches a kurr in volume become ritually impure?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a foundational ruling in Shia fiqh: water that reaches the volume of a kurr cannot be rendered ritually impure (najis) by any contaminant that falls into it. The kurr is the critical threshold separating 'abundant water' (al-ma' al-kathir), which resists najasah, from 'little water' (al-ma' al-qalil), which becomes impure upon contact; Shia jurists define it as approximately 36 cubic handspans (roughly 377 liters), and this hadith is among the primary textual foundations for that ruling.
